description: My password expired over the weekend and I can't log into my laptop. Please reset it.
I forgot my network password after coming back from PTO. The self-service reset link says my security questions are not set up.
Password expired and the reset portal keeps timing out. I need to get into email for a customer call.
resolution: Verified caller identity via employee ID and manager name. Reset AD password, set change-at-next-logon, confirmed user logged in.
Reset password and enrolled user in self-service password reset so they can reset it themselves next time.

kb.title: Resetting an expired or forgotten network password
kb.symptoms: User cannot log into Windows, VPN, or email because the network password is expired or forgotten.
kb.cause: Network passwords expire every 90 days. Users who have not enrolled in self-service password reset (SSPR) cannot reset their own password.
steps: Verify the caller's identity with employee ID plus one additional factor (manager name or last 4 of phone on file).
In Active Directory Users and Computers, reset the password and check 'User must change password at next logon'.
Have the user log in while on the phone to confirm.
If the user is not enrolled in SSPR, walk them through enrollment at the self-service portal.

description: My account got locked this morning and now it keeps locking every few minutes even after I unlock it.
I'm locked out of my computer. I think I typed the wrong password too many times.
Account locked out again. This is the third time this week, I changed my password on Monday.
resolution: Unlocked account. Lockout source traced to old credentials cached on user's phone mail app. User updated password on phone, no further lockouts.
Unlocked AD account and cleared stale credentials from Windows Credential Manager. Monitored for 30 min, no repeat lockouts.

kb.title: Recurring AD account lockouts after a password change
kb.symptoms: User's account locks repeatedly, often within minutes of being unlocked, usually shortly after a password change.
kb.cause: A device or saved credential (phone mail app, mapped drive, Credential Manager entry, disconnected RDP session) keeps retrying the old password.
steps: Unlock the account in AD.
Use the lockout status tool to identify the domain controller and source workstation of the bad password attempts.
Ask the user to update the password on their mobile mail app and remove stale entries from Windows Credential Manager.
Log off any disconnected RDP sessions under the user's name.
Monitor for 30 minutes before resolving.

short: Got a new phone, MFA not working
Authenticator app lost after phone upgrade
description: I upgraded my phone yesterday and the Authenticator app didn't transfer. Now I can't approve sign-in requests and I'm blocked from email and Teams.
MFA push notifications stopped arriving. I reinstalled the app but it doesn't show my work account anymore.
Traded in my old phone and lost the authenticator. Need to re-register MFA so I can sign in.
resolution: Verified identity via manager callback. Revoked old MFA registrations and issued a Temporary Access Pass. User re-registered Authenticator on new phone.
Cleared MFA methods for the user and required re-registration. User completed setup and confirmed sign-in to Outlook and Teams.

kb.title: Re-registering MFA after a phone replacement
kb.symptoms: User cannot complete MFA because the Authenticator app was lost or not transferred to a new device.
kb.cause: Authenticator registrations are bound to the original device and are not always restored from phone backups.
steps: Verify identity using a manager callback. Do not rely on information the caller provides alone.
In the identity portal, revoke existing MFA sessions and delete the old Authenticator registration.
Issue a Temporary Access Pass valid for 1 hour.
Guide the user through registering the Authenticator app at the security info page.
Confirm a successful sign-in before resolving.

short: Please add me to the {share} share
description: I just transferred to the {share} team and need access to the {share} shared drive. My manager approved this.
Getting 'access denied' when I open the {share} folder. My coworkers on the same team can open it.
New hire, need read/write on the {share} share to do my job. Manager is copied.
resolution: Confirmed manager approval. Added user to the {share} RW security group. User must log off and back on for the group membership to apply; confirmed access.
Access granted via {share} data owner approval. Added to AD group and verified user can open the folder after re-login.

kb.title: Granting access to a departmental shared drive
kb.symptoms: User receives 'access denied' on a departmental shared folder or requests access after a transfer or new hire.
kb.cause: Shared drive permissions are managed through AD security groups. The user is not a member of the group, or their Kerberos token has not refreshed since being added.
steps: Confirm approval from the user's manager AND the share's data owner (listed in the file services catalog).
Add the user to the correct RO or RW security group. Do not grant permissions directly on the folder.
Tell the user to log off and log back on (or run klist purge) so the new group membership applies.
Confirm access and resolve.

description: When I click the {app} tile it redirects back to the login page over and over.
{app} shows 'user is not assigned to this application' when I try to sign in. I used it last week without a problem.
I get an SSO error when opening {app}. Tried a different browser, same issue.
resolution: User was missing the {app} app assignment after a department change reset group memberships. Re-added to the {app} access group; login confirmed.
Cleared a stale SAML session and corrected the user's email attribute mismatch between the IdP and {app}. Login working.

kb.title: Troubleshooting SSO failures for SaaS applications
kb.symptoms: User gets redirect loops, 'user not assigned', or SAML errors when opening a SaaS app from the SSO portal.
kb.cause: Common causes: the app assignment was removed after an HR department change, the user's email/UPN attribute does not match the app, or a stale browser session.
steps: Check the user's app assignments in the IdP admin console.
If the assignment is missing, re-add the user to the app's access group (department changes can remove it).
Compare the user's UPN/email in the IdP with the username in the target app.
Have the user clear cookies or try an InPrivate window.
Escalate to the application team only if the IdP shows a successful SAML assertion.

short: Unable to connect to VPN from home
description: Working from home today and GlobalProtect says '{error_code}'. My internet is fine otherwise.
VPN connects for a minute and then drops. I can't reach any internal sites or shared drives.
GlobalProtect is stuck on 'connecting' since this morning. Rebooted twice already.
resolution: GlobalProtect client was on the new version with a corrupted portal config. Cleared the cached portal settings and re-entered the portal address; VPN connected.
Rolled back GlobalProtect client to the previous stable version per known issue with the latest build. Connection stable.
Home router was blocking UDP 4501. Switched the client to SSL fallback; user connected successfully.

kb.title: GlobalProtect VPN fails to connect or drops after a client upgrade
kb.symptoms: GlobalProtect shows 'Gateway not responding', stays on 'connecting', or disconnects within minutes. Often seen right after an automatic client upgrade.
kb.cause: Known issue: the upgraded client can keep a corrupted cached portal configuration. Some home routers also block the UDP 4501 IPSec tunnel.
steps: Confirm the user has general internet access.
Check the GlobalProtect client version. If it is the latest build, clear the cached portal: Settings > remove portal, then re-add the portal address.
If the problem persists, force SSL fallback or roll back to the previous stable client via the software portal.
If multiple users report the issue at the same time, check the gateway status dashboard and link to the parent problem record.

description: Wi-Fi in the {area} at {site} drops every few minutes. Several people are having the same problem.
My laptop keeps disconnecting from the corporate Wi-Fi. It's fine when I plug into a cable.
Wireless is extremely slow in the {area}. Teams calls keep freezing.
resolution: Access point serving the {area} was down after a PoE switch port error. Bounced the port; AP came back online and clients reconnected.
Found channel interference from a neighboring AP. Adjusted RF channel plan for the {area}; throughput back to normal.
Laptop wireless driver was outdated. Updated driver via software center; connection stable.

kb.title: Diagnosing Wi-Fi drops at a corporate site
kb.symptoms: Users in one area lose Wi-Fi intermittently or see very slow speeds. Wired connections work.
kb.cause: Usually an offline or overloaded access point, RF channel interference, or an outdated client wireless driver.
steps: Determine scope: one user (likely the client) or many users in one area (likely infrastructure).
For area-wide issues, check the wireless controller for AP status and client counts in that zone.
If an AP is down, check the PoE switch port and bounce it.
For single users, update the wireless driver and forget/rejoin the corporate SSID.

description: Nobody on our floor at {site} can reach anything, internal or internet. Phones are down too.
Everything stopped loading about 10 minutes ago. Whole office at {site} is affected.
Network completely down at {site}. Can't print, can't get email, can't reach any apps.
resolution: Core switch at {site} failed a supervisor module. Failed over to redundant supervisor and replaced the faulty module. Linked to parent incident and problem record.
Upstream fiber cut on carrier circuit. Traffic failed over to backup circuit; carrier repaired primary. Resolved via parent incident.

kb.title: Handling a site-wide network outage
kb.symptoms: Many users at one site report no connectivity at the same time: no internal apps, no internet, and often no desk phones.
kb.cause: Core switch failure, upstream carrier circuit outage, or power issue in the main distribution frame.
steps: Check the monitoring dashboard for the site's core switch and WAN circuit status.
Create a single parent incident and relate every new user report as a child. Do not work each ticket separately.
Engage the on-call network engineer and open a carrier ticket if the WAN circuit is down.
Post a status update on the service portal banner.
After restoration, resolve all child incidents through the parent and open a problem record.

description: Internet has been very slow all afternoon at {site}. Websites take 30+ seconds to load.
Downloading anything from SharePoint is crawling. Colleagues say it's slow for them too.
External websites are slow but internal apps seem OK.
resolution: WAN circuit at {site} was saturated by a large backup job running during business hours. Rescheduled the job to off-hours; utilization normal.
Proxy node in the pool was degraded. Removed it from rotation; browsing speed restored.

kb.title: Investigating slow internet at a site
kb.symptoms: Users at a site report slow web browsing or downloads. Internal applications may be unaffected.
kb.cause: WAN circuit saturation (often from backups or large syncs), a degraded proxy node, or ISP issues.
steps: Check WAN circuit utilization for the site in the monitoring tool.
Identify top talkers. Reschedule backup or sync jobs running during business hours.
Check proxy pool health and remove degraded nodes.
Open a carrier ticket if the circuit shows errors or packet loss.

short: Laptop fan loud and everything slow
description: My laptop has gotten really slow over the last couple weeks. Excel freezes and it takes forever to open anything.
Computer is freezing multiple times a day. I have to hard restart it.
Startup takes 10+ minutes and the fan is running loud all the time.
resolution: Disk was 98% full due to a large local OneDrive cache. Enabled Files On-Demand and cleared temp files; performance restored.
Laptop had only 8 GB RAM and heavy workloads. Scheduled hardware refresh to 16 GB model; provided loaner in the meantime.
Endpoint security full scan was stuck in a loop. Updated agent to the current version; CPU usage normal.

kb.title: Laptop performance troubleshooting
kb.symptoms: Laptop is slow, freezes, boots slowly, or runs the fan constantly.
kb.cause: Common causes: low disk space (often OneDrive cache), insufficient RAM for the workload, a stuck security agent scan, or an aging device.
steps: Check free disk space. If below 10%, enable OneDrive Files On-Demand and clear temp files.
Check Task Manager for processes with high CPU/RAM. Update the endpoint security agent if its scan is stuck.
Check device age and RAM. Devices older than 4 years or with 8 GB RAM qualify for refresh.
Run hardware diagnostics if freezes continue.

description: My laptop won't power on at all this morning. Charger light is on but nothing happens.
Getting a blue screen every time I start my computer. It restarts in a loop.
Laptop is asking for a BitLocker recovery key and I don't know what that is.
resolution: Provided BitLocker recovery key after identity verification. Triggered by a BIOS update; suspended and resumed BitLocker to prevent recurrence.
Motherboard failure confirmed by diagnostics. Swapped for a loaner and opened vendor warranty case; data restored from OneDrive.
Bad Windows update caused boot loop. Uninstalled update from recovery environment; device boots normally.

kb.title: Laptop does not boot or shows BitLocker recovery
kb.symptoms: Laptop does not power on, blue-screens during boot, or prompts for a BitLocker recovery key.
kb.cause: BitLocker recovery is usually triggered by BIOS/firmware updates or hardware changes. Boot loops are often caused by a failed Windows update. No power usually means a hardware failure.
steps: For BitLocker prompts: verify identity, retrieve the recovery key from the device record, and read it to the user. Afterwards, suspend and resume BitLocker.
For boot loops: boot to the recovery environment and uninstall the latest quality update.
For no power: try a known-good charger and a battery reset, then run vendor diagnostics.
If hardware has failed, provide a loaner and open a warranty case.

short: Dock keyboard and mouse stopped working
description: When I plug into my docking station neither of my monitors turns on. Laptop screen works fine.
Keyboard and mouse connected to the dock stopped responding. They work if I plug them directly into the laptop.
Only one of my two external monitors shows anything since yesterday.
resolution: Updated dock firmware and Thunderbolt driver; both monitors detected.
Dock power supply was failing. Replaced dock from desk-side stock.

kb.title: USB-C dock or external monitor issues
kb.symptoms: External monitors are blank or keyboard/mouse on the dock do not work, while the laptop works on its own.
kb.cause: Outdated dock firmware or Thunderbolt drivers, a failing dock power supply, or a bad cable.
steps: Power-cycle the dock by unplugging its power for 30 seconds.
Update dock firmware and the laptop's Thunderbolt/USB-C drivers from the software center.
Swap the display cable and test each monitor individually.
Replace the dock if the issue persists.

description: I need {software} for a project. It isn't listed in Software Center.
Tried installing {software} from Software Center and it fails at 50% with an error.
Manager approved {software} for me. Please install it on my laptop.
resolution: Verified license availability and approval. Deployed {software} to user's device via Software Center; confirmed launch.
Install was failing due to a pending reboot. Rebooted device and re-ran deployment; {software} installed successfully.

kb.title: Installing software not available in Software Center
kb.symptoms: User requests software that is not self-service, or a Software Center install fails.
kb.cause: Licensed software requires approval and a license assignment before deployment. Failed installs are often caused by a pending reboot or low disk space.
steps: Check whether the software is on the approved catalog and whether a license is available.
Obtain manager approval for licensed software.
Add the device to the software's deployment collection.
For failed installs, reboot, confirm at least 10 GB free disk space, and retry.

description: Printer {printer_id} shows offline for everyone on our floor. Jobs just sit in the queue.
My print jobs to {printer_id} disappear and nothing comes out.
I can't find printer {printer_id} when I try to add it on my laptop.
resolution: Print spooler on print server hung. Restarted spooler service and cleared stuck jobs; {printer_id} printing.
Printer {printer_id} had a paper jam and a stale DHCP lease. Cleared jam and set a DHCP reservation; back online.

kb.title: Office printer offline or jobs stuck in queue
kb.symptoms: Printer shows offline, jobs stay in the queue, or the printer cannot be added.
kb.cause: Hung print spooler on the print server, a printer IP change (no DHCP reservation), or a hardware fault such as a paper jam.
steps: Check the printer panel for errors or jams.
Ping the printer's IP. If the IP changed, create a DHCP reservation and update the port.
Restart the print spooler on the print server and clear stuck jobs.
Have users re-add the printer from the print server if it is missing.

description: Outlook says 'Disconnected' at the bottom and I haven't received any email since 7am.
My inbox isn't updating. People say they sent me emails but I don't see them. Webmail shows them.
Outlook is stuck on 'Updating this folder' and won't send anything from my outbox.
resolution: Corrupted OST file. Rebuilt Outlook profile; mailbox resynced.
Exchange Online service incident affected mail flow. Resolved after vendor mitigation; linked to parent incident.
Mailbox was over quota. Enabled archive policy and cleared large items; sync resumed.

kb.title: Outlook not syncing or disconnected
kb.symptoms: Outlook shows Disconnected or 'Updating this folder', new mail does not arrive, or items stay in the Outbox.
kb.cause: Corrupted local OST cache, mailbox over quota, or an Exchange Online service incident.
steps: Check the Microsoft 365 service health dashboard for an active Exchange incident. If there is one, link to the parent incident.
Check whether webmail works. If it does, the problem is local to Outlook.
Check mailbox quota and enable archiving if the mailbox is near its limit.
Rebuild the Outlook profile to recreate the OST.

short: People can't hear me on Teams
description: In Teams meetings nobody can hear me. My headset works fine in other apps.
Teams doesn't detect my headset. It only lets me use the laptop speakers.
Audio cuts in and out on every Teams call since yesterday.
resolution: Teams was using the wrong default device. Set headset as device in Teams settings and Windows sound settings; audio working.
Cleared Teams cache and updated headset firmware; microphone detected.

kb.title: Teams audio and headset problems
kb.symptoms: Others cannot hear the user in Teams, the headset is not detected, or audio drops during calls.
kb.cause: Wrong audio device selected in Teams or Windows, outdated headset firmware, or a corrupted Teams cache.
steps: In Teams, go to Settings > Devices and select the headset for both speaker and microphone.
Check Windows sound settings and microphone privacy permissions.
Clear the Teams cache and restart Teams.
Update headset firmware using the vendor utility.

short: Shared mailbox {mailbox} not showing in Outlook
description: I joined the team that manages the {mailbox} mailbox. Please give me access so it shows in Outlook.
I was given access to {mailbox} but it doesn't appear in my Outlook folder list.
I can read {mailbox} but I get an error when I try to send as it.
resolution: Granted Full Access and Send As on {mailbox} with owner approval. Mailbox automapped after Outlook restart.
Access existed but automapping was disabled. Added mailbox manually in Outlook account settings.

kb.title: Shared mailbox access and Send As permissions
kb.symptoms: User needs access to a shared mailbox, the mailbox does not appear in Outlook, or 'Send As' fails.
kb.cause: Full Access and Send As are separate permissions. Automapping can take up to an hour or may be disabled.
steps: Get approval from the shared mailbox owner.
Grant Full Access (read) and Send As (send) separately in the Exchange admin center.
Wait up to 60 minutes for automapping, then restart Outlook.
If it still does not appear, add the mailbox manually under Account Settings > More Settings > Advanced.

short: I clicked a link in a weird email
description: Got an email claiming to be from a carrier asking me to log in to view an invoice. The link looks strange.
I clicked a link in an email about a package delivery before I realized it was probably fake. I didn't enter a password.
Several of us got an email asking us to update direct deposit info. Looks like phishing.
resolution: Confirmed phishing. Purged message from all mailboxes, blocked sender domain and URL. User did not enter credentials; no further action.
User clicked link and entered credentials. Forced password reset, revoked sessions, and reviewed sign-in logs; no malicious activity found.

kb.title: Responding to a reported phishing email
kb.symptoms: User reports a suspicious email, or says they clicked a link or opened an attachment from one.
kb.cause: Phishing campaigns often impersonate carriers, invoices, or HR/payroll.
steps: Ask the user to use the 'Report Phishing' button. Do not forward the email.
Analyze headers and URLs in the email security console.
If malicious, purge the message org-wide and block the sender and URL.
If the user entered credentials: reset the password, revoke sessions, and review sign-in logs.
If an attachment was opened: isolate the device and run a full EDR scan.

description: A security popup appeared saying a threat was found and quarantined. Not sure if I need to do anything.
My browser keeps redirecting to strange sites and I'm getting pop-ups.
Got a notification from the security software after opening a zip file from email.
resolution: EDR quarantined adware from a browser extension. Removed extension, full scan clean, reset browser settings.
Device isolated via EDR after a malicious macro execution. Reimaged laptop and reset user credentials as a precaution.

kb.title: Handling endpoint malware alerts
kb.symptoms: User sees an EDR/antivirus alert, browser redirects, or unexpected pop-ups.
kb.cause: Malicious attachments, macros, or unwanted browser extensions.
steps: Review the alert in the EDR console and determine severity.
For high severity, isolate the device immediately through EDR.
Remove the offending files or extensions and run a full scan.
Reimage if persistence is found, and reset the user's credentials.
Document indicators of compromise in the security incident.

description: My laptop was stolen from my car last night. I filed a police report.
I think I left my work phone in a rideshare. It has email and Teams on it.
Lost my laptop while traveling. It was locked but I'm worried about the data.
resolution: Issued remote wipe via MDM, disabled device in directory, revoked user sessions and reset password. Replacement device ordered.
Device located by user before wipe executed. Wipe canceled; sessions revoked and password reset as precaution.

kb.title: Lost or stolen company device
kb.symptoms: User reports a lost or stolen laptop or phone.
kb.cause: N/A. This is a security response procedure.
steps: Record where and when the device was lost and whether a police report was filed.
Issue a remote lock/wipe through MDM and disable the device object in the directory.
Revoke all user sessions and reset the password.
Confirm BitLocker was enabled on the device (for compliance reporting).
Order a replacement device through End User Computing.

description: SAP is extremely slow today. Transaction {tcode} takes minutes to respond and we're trying to close the month.
Running {tcode} times out. Finance needs these numbers for close tomorrow.
The whole accounting team is seeing SAP hang. Nothing is finishing.
resolution: Heavy month-end batch jobs overlapped with interactive use. Rescheduled non-critical batch jobs and added dialog work processes; response times normal.
Long-running custom report was locking tables. Terminated the job and scheduled it in background overnight.

kb.title: SAP performance degradation during month-end close
kb.symptoms: SAP transactions are slow or time out, especially in the last days of the month when finance runs close activities.
kb.cause: Month-end batch jobs and heavy reports compete with interactive users for work processes and database resources.
steps: Check SM50/SM66 for long-running work processes and SM37 for active batch jobs.
Reschedule non-critical batch jobs outside business hours.
Temporarily increase dialog work processes using operation modes.
Identify custom reports that lock tables and move them to background execution.
Engage the DBA team if database wait times are high.

short: Purchase order not routing to approver
description: Purchase order {po_number} has been waiting for approval for 3 days. My manager says they never got it in their inbox.
PO {po_number} shows 'in release' but no approver is listed.
The approver for my department left the company and now all our POs are stuck.
resolution: Approver in release strategy had left the company. Updated release strategy with new approver and restarted workflow for {po_number}.
Workflow item was in error due to missing cost center. Corrected the cost center and restarted the workflow; PO released.

kb.title: Purchase order stuck in SAP release workflow
kb.symptoms: PO stays 'in release' with no approver action, or the approver never receives the workitem.
kb.cause: The approver in the release strategy left or changed roles, or the workflow errored because of missing master data such as a cost center.
steps: Check the workflow log (SWIA) for the PO's workitem status.
If the workitem is in error, fix the master data issue and restart the workflow.
If the approver is invalid, update the release strategy assignment with HR/finance approval.
Forward or restart the workitem to the correct approver.

description: Trying to post vendor invoice {invoice} in MIRO and getting '{sap_error}'.
Invoice {invoice} is blocked for payment and the vendor is calling about it.
Getting error '{sap_error}' on several carrier invoices this morning.
resolution: Error '{sap_error}': Posting period for the company code was not opened. Opened the period in OB52 with finance approval; invoice posted.
Price variance exceeded tolerance. Buyer confirmed the correct price; released the blocked invoice in MRBR.

kb.title: Common SAP invoice posting errors (MIRO)
kb.symptoms: Vendor invoice cannot be posted in MIRO or is blocked for payment.
kb.cause: Posting period closed, price/quantity variance beyond tolerance, or goods receipt/invoice receipt mismatch.
steps: 'Posting period not open': confirm with finance, then open the period in OB52.
'Tolerance limit exceeded': confirm the price with the buyer, then release in MRBR.
'GR/IR mismatch': confirm the goods receipt was posted for the invoiced quantity.
Document the resolution for audit purposes.

description: The {report} report times out after 5 minutes. It used to run in under 30 seconds.
Power BI dashboard for {report} shows 'query timeout' when refreshing.
Our team can't pull the {report} report today. The page just spins.
resolution: Execution plan regression on {server} after stats update. Forced previous plan via Query Store and updated statistics; report runs in 20s.
Missing index on shipment date column after table growth. Added covering index on {server}; query time reduced from 6 min to 15s.

kb.title: Report queries timing out on reporting SQL servers
kb.symptoms: A report or dashboard that used to be fast now times out or takes minutes.
kb.cause: Query plan regression after a statistics update, or a missing index as tables grow.
steps: Identify the query in Query Store or with sp_WhoIsActive while the report runs.
Compare current and historical execution plans. If the plan regressed, force the last known good plan.
Check for missing index recommendations and table growth.
Update statistics and test the report.
Create a change request for any new indexes.

short: Replication lag alert on reporting DB
description: All our dashboards are showing data from yesterday afternoon. Nothing new since then.
Monitoring alert: replication latency to reporting replica exceeds 2 hours.
The shipment numbers in reports don't match SAP. Reporting seems several hours behind.
resolution: Log reader agent stalled after a large batch update. Restarted the agent; replication caught up within 40 minutes.
Replica disk IO saturated by an index rebuild. Paused the maintenance job; latency back under 1 minute.

kb.title: Reporting replica replication lag
kb.symptoms: Reports and dashboards show stale data, or monitoring alerts on replication latency.
kb.cause: A stalled log reader or distribution agent, large batch transactions, or IO saturation on the replica.
steps: Check replication monitor for latency and agent status.
Restart stalled log reader or distribution agents.
Check replica disk IO. Pause maintenance jobs if they are saturating IO.
Tell reporting users the expected catch-up time.

description: Customers are calling saying the {web_app} shows a 500 error.
{web_app} is returning 502 Bad Gateway intermittently. Synthetic monitor is failing.
Our carriers can't use {web_app} to book loads. It errors out after login.
resolution: Latest deployment of {web_app} introduced a connection pool leak. Rolled back to previous release; error rate back to baseline.
Autoscaling hit the max instance count during a traffic spike. Raised the limit and added a CPU-based scaling policy.

kb.title: Customer-facing web app returning 5xx errors
kb.symptoms: A customer-facing application returns 500/502/503 errors, or synthetic monitors fail.
kb.cause: A bad deployment, exhausted connection pools, autoscaling limits, or failing downstream dependencies.
steps: Check the deployment history. If a release happened within the last 24 hours, consider rolling back first.
Review application logs and APM traces for the failing endpoint.
Check instance counts against autoscaling limits, and check database connection pool metrics.
Post customer communication through the status page if the outage lasts more than 15 minutes.

description: Browsers show 'Your connection is not private' when opening {web_app}.
Partner integrations to {web_app} are failing with TLS certificate errors since this morning.
Customers report a security warning when visiting {web_app}.
resolution: TLS certificate for {web_app} expired because auto-renewal failed on DNS validation. Renewed certificate, deployed to load balancer, and added expiry alerting at 30/14/7 days.
Intermediate certificate missing from chain after renewal. Deployed full chain; clients validating successfully.

kb.title: Expired or misconfigured TLS certificate
kb.symptoms: Browsers show certificate warnings or API clients fail TLS handshakes.
kb.cause: Certificate expired because auto-renewal failed, or the intermediate chain is incomplete.
steps: Check the certificate expiry and chain with an SSL checker.
Renew the certificate and deploy it with the full chain to the load balancer.
Find out why auto-renewal failed (DNS validation, permissions).
Add expiry monitoring at 30, 14, and 7 days.

description: Scanner {scanner_id} at {dock} keeps saying 'host not reachable' and scans are not uploading to WMS.
Several RF guns at {dock} freeze when we scan pallets. We're falling behind on receiving.
Handheld {scanner_id} shows scans as pending and they never reach the system.
resolution: Scanner roaming between APs at {dock} dropped the WMS session. Adjusted roaming threshold in the MDM profile; sync stable.
Handheld {scanner_id} had an expired Wi-Fi certificate. Re-enrolled device in MDM; pending scans uploaded.

kb.title: Warehouse handheld scanners not syncing to WMS
kb.symptoms: RF handhelds show 'host not reachable', freeze while scanning, or keep scans pending.
kb.cause: Aggressive roaming between access points drops the WMS session, the device Wi-Fi certificate expired, or the WMS app server session limit was reached.
steps: Check the device in MDM: last check-in time, certificate expiry, and app version.
If several devices in one zone are affected, check AP health for that zone with Network Operations.
Apply the warehouse roaming profile (higher roaming threshold) via MDM.
Re-enroll devices whose certificates have expired.
Confirm pending scans uploaded to WMS before resolving.

description: Label printer {label_printer} stopped printing shipping labels. Trucks are waiting at the dock.
Labels come out blank or half printed from {label_printer}.
Shipping labels print with garbled characters instead of barcodes.
resolution: Printhead dirty and ribbon misaligned on {label_printer}. Cleaned printhead, recalibrated media; labels printing correctly.
Printer lost its ZPL language setting after a firmware reset. Set language to ZPL and recalibrated.

kb.title: Shipping label printer issues (Zebra)
kb.symptoms: Label printer is offline or prints blank, faded, or garbled labels.
kb.cause: Dirty printhead, ribbon or media misalignment, the printer language reset from ZPL, or a network drop.
steps: Check the printer display for errors and confirm media and ribbon are loaded correctly.
Run media calibration (hold the feed button until it flashes twice).
For garbled output, confirm the printer language is set to ZPL.
Clean the printhead with an isopropyl pen.
If the printer is offline, ping it and check its switch port.

short: Orders not dropping to the floor

resolution: Wave {wave} failed on an item with missing dimensions. Corrected item master data and re-released the wave.
SAP-to-WMS order interface queue was stuck. Restarted the integration listener; orders flowed and wave released.

kb.title: WMS wave fails to release or pick tasks are not generated
kb.symptoms: Wave release fails or hangs, and no pick tasks are created for the floor.
kb.cause: Items with missing master data (dimensions/weight), a stuck SAP-to-WMS order interface, or allocation failures from inventory mismatches.
steps: Check the wave's error log in WMS for the failing order or item.
Fix missing item master data and re-release the wave.
Check the SAP-to-WMS integration queue depth. Restart the listener if it is stuck.
Engage the ERP team if orders are not being sent from SAP.

short: Email not working on my phone
Company Portal says device not compliant
Outlook mobile keeps asking to sign in
description: Outlook on my iPhone stopped syncing and says my device is not compliant.
Trying to set up my new Android phone and Company Portal enrollment fails.
Outlook mobile keeps asking me to sign in over and over.
resolution: Device was non-compliant due to an outdated OS. User updated iOS, device re-checked compliance, and Outlook synced.
Enrollment failed because device limit reached. Removed old device records from MDM; new phone enrolled.

kb.title: Mobile email and MDM compliance issues
kb.symptoms: Outlook mobile stops syncing, reports non-compliance, or loops on sign-in. MDM enrollment fails.
kb.cause: Outdated OS version below the compliance policy, device enrollment limit reached, or stale device records.
steps: Check the device's compliance status and reason in MDM.
Have the user update the phone OS to the minimum supported version.
Remove stale device records if the user is at the enrollment limit.
Have the user run 'Check status' in Company Portal, then reopen Outlook.
